title: Speech coaching that treats words like body language
summary:
The sticky idea: @christineist says @myceliummage’s speech coaching works like “synesthesia for emotion-language”—your sentences have *shape, texture, and movement*, and the “weird texture” is basically your feelings leaking through the grammar.

What kicked it off was Christine announcing she’s doing 6 weeks of coaching with Mage and live-threading the process. The thread peaks when she explains the core move from Session 1: hunt for {1} “Negation” (“not,” “but,” “un-”), delete it, and watch what emotion was hiding in the folds. Her before/after example is the tell: the cleaned-up version forces an uncomfortable specificity (“on earth… it may warm you for a moment before leaving you hollow and blue”), which is exactly the point—your evasive sentence structure is often self-protection. Mage’s broader claim (as filtered through Christine) is that “smooth” speech is words aligned with underlying emotion; “chaotic patterning” (knots/arrows/passive aggression vibes) is misalignment.

The rest of the arc is community validation and riffing rather than fighting: @rickbenger tries to name the thing as “martial speech,” a mixed-modality practice with discipline + forms + movement; @chercher_ai does the solemn “Everything is communication”; @loopholekid just calls Mage’s distillation “INCREDIBLE.” And then it kind of dissolves into playful application, with @zencephalon taking “shape of language” literally and going full typography debate (“U” vs “you,” equalizing ‘U’ and ‘I’). You’d care if you write, pitch, flirt, negotiate, or do therapy-adjacent work—because this frames style tics (negation, hedging, passive aggression) as *diagnostic signals* you can train, not personality traits you’re stuck with.
